title: Borel Weil and Borel Weil Bott

items.title: Sections of an associated line bundle as equivariant functions
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex semisimple affine algebraic group with Borel $B=T\ltimes U$ and flag variety $X=G/B$ of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]] and [[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]], and let $\mathcal L_\lambda=G\times^B\mathbb C_{-\lambda}$ be the Borel-character equivariant line bundle of [[def-borel-character-equivariant-line-bundle]]. Restriction along the $B$-torsor $G\to X$ of [[lem-semisimple-flag-torsor-zariski-charts]] identifies the global sections of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ with the regular functions on $G$ satisfying $f(gb)=\lambda(b)f(g)$: $$H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong\{f\in\mathcal O(G):f(gb)=\lambda(b)f(g)\text{ for all }g\in G,\ b\in B\},$$ an isomorphism natural in $\lambda$. Under it the left translation action $(g\cdot f)(x)=f(g^{-1}x)$ corresponds to the $G$-action on sections induced by the equivariant structure, and evaluation at the identity, $\mathrm{ev}_1(f)=f(1)$, is a $B$-equivariant linear functional onto the fibre $\mathbb C_{-\lambda}$ of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ at $eB$.
items.strategy: Construct inverse maps. A section $s$ of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ pulls back along the projection $\pi:G\to X$ to a $B$-equivariant map $\pi^*\mathcal L_\lambda\to\mathbb C$; on the total space of the associated bundle this is a regular function $f$ on $G$ with $f(gb)=\lambda(b)f(g)$, because the gluing relation is $(gb,v)\sim(g,\lambda(b)^{-1}v)$ and the section is constant along the second factor. In the other direction a regular $f$ with this functional equation descends to a section: the local trivializations supplied by [[lem-semisimple-flag-torsor-zariski-charts]] have transition functions given exactly by the same functional equation, so the local sections $U\mapsto[\sigma(x),f(\sigma(x))]$ agree on overlaps. On the left, the equivariant structure transports the fibre above $x$ to the fibre above $gx$, which on functions is the stated left translation. Evaluation at $1$ reads off the fibre at $eB$ and is $B$-equivariant because $(b\cdot f)(1)=f(b^{-1})=\lambda(b)^{-1}f(1)$.

items.title: The cohomology of a Borel-character line bundle is a rational G-module
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In the setting of [[lem-sections-of-an-associated-line-bundle-as-equivariant-functions]], the $G$-equivariant structure of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ induces for every $i\ge0$ a natural linear action of $G$ on $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)$; for $i=0$ it is the left translation action on the function model, and for every $G$-equivariant isomorphism $\phi:\mathcal L_\lambda\to\mathcal L_\mu$ the induced maps $H^i(\phi)$ are $G$-equivariant. Each $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)$ is a finite-dimensional rational $G$-module, meaning that its action homomorphism $G\to\operatorname{GL}(H^i(X,\mathcal{L}_\lambda))$ is a morphism of algebraic groups, and hence differentiates to a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module. On $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)$ the action is left translation $(g\cdot f)(g')=f(g^{-1}g')$ in the function model. The canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal L_\lambda\otimes\mathcal L_\mu\cong\mathcal L_{\lambda+\mu}$ and $\mathcal L_\lambda^\vee\cong\mathcal L_{-\lambda}$ of [[def-borel-character-equivariant-line-bundle]] are $G$-equivariant.
items.strategy: For each g, the bundle action gives Phi_g:L_lambda->a_g^*L_lambda and rho_i(g)=H^i(a_{g^{-1}}^*Phi_g) composed with pullback by a_{g^{-1}}; the corrected cocycle proves the left action and recovers left translation on H^0. To show rationality, use A(g,x)=(g,g^{-1}x) on GxX and its induced line-bundle map. A finite affine cover of projective X and its product cover compute the cohomology as O(G) tensor H^i(X,L_lambda) by the published Cech comparison and affine quasi-coherent module equivalence. The universal action gives an O(G)-linear endomorphism of this module, so its matrix coefficients are regular; the action law makes it an algebraic representation. Proper coherent cohomology gives finite dimensionality, and the tensor/dual bundle maps are equivariant.

items.title: A $U^-$-invariant section is determined on the big cell
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$ and let $f\in H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)$, regarded as a regular function on $G$ with $f(gb)=\lambda(b)f(g)$. If $f$ is invariant under left translation by $U^-$ (equivalently, if $x\cdot f=0$ for every $x$ in the negative nilradical $\mathfrak n^-$), then $$f(u^-b)=\lambda(b)f(1)\qquad(u^-\in U^-,\ b\in B).$$ Consequently $f$ is determined by its value $f(1)$, the space of left-$U^-$-invariant sections of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ has dimension at most $1$, and every nonzero such section spans the $T$-weight space of weight $-\lambda$, that is $t\cdot f=\lambda(t)^{-1}f$ for all $t\in T$.
items.strategy: By [[lem-semisimple-opposite-borel-big-cell]] the multiplication map $U^-\times B\to G$ is an isomorphism onto a dense open subset $\Omega$. A section that is fixed by $U^-$ satisfies $f(u^-b)=f(1\cdot u^-b)=f(b)=\lambda(b)f(1)$, since $f(u^-\cdot 1)=f(1)$; so its values on the dense open $\Omega$ are determined by $f(1)$. Two regular functions agreeing on a dense open subset of the irreducible variety $G$ agree everywhere, so $f$ is determined by $f(1)$; linearity gives dimension at most $1$. For the weight, compute in the function model: $(t\cdot f)(1)=f(t^{-1})=\lambda(t^{-1})f(1)=\lambda(t)^{-1}f(1)$, so $t\cdot f=\lambda(t)^{-1}f$ because both sides are the unique $U^-$-invariant section with that value at $1$. The equivalence of $U^-$-invariance with annihilation by $\mathfrak n^-$ is differentiation of the unipotent group action, $U^-$ being connected.

items.title: The dominant Borel-Weil section extends from the big cell
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be a dominant integral weight. Then there exists a regular function $v\in\mathcal O(G)$ with $v(gb)=\lambda(b)v(g)$ for all $g\in G$, $b\in B$, and $v(1)=1$. Equivalently, $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\neq0$ for every dominant integral $\lambda$.
items.strategy: On the big cell $\Omega=U^-B\cong U^-\times B$ of [[lem-semisimple-opposite-borel-big-cell]] define $v(u^-b)=\lambda(b)$; this is a regular function on $\Omega$ satisfying the functional equation and $v(1)=1$. View $v$ as a rational function on the affine variety $G$; by [[thm-principal-subvariety-codimension-one]] and the Bruhat decomposition of [[thm-flag-variety-bruhat-cell-decomposition]] and [[lem-semisimple-bruhat-double-cosets]], a pole divisor of $v$ is supported on the closures of the Bruhat cells of positive codimension, and it suffices to exclude poles along the codimension-one cells $\overline{Bs_\alpha B}$, $\alpha$ simple; these are the only lower covers of the big cell by [[lem-bruhat-covers-are-reflection-covers]]. Fix $\alpha$ and the rank-one subgroup $\varphi_\alpha:SL_2\to G$ of [[lem-semisimple-rank-one-sl2-root-homomorphism]] with unipotent subgroups $U_{\pm\alpha}$ of [[lem-semisimple-root-exponential-algebraic-subgroups]]. Near the generic point of the cell $\overline{Bs_\alpha B}$, the pole order of $v$ is governed by the pullback of $v$ to the big cell of $SL_2$: in the coordinates $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{pmatrix}$ with $c\ne0$, the function $\varphi_\alpha^*v$ equals $a^{\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle}$ (the big cell factors as $u^-(z)\,b^-$ with $b^-=\mathrm{diag}(e,e^{-1})$ and the first matrix entry $a=e$), which is regular exactly when the integer $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ is nonnegative. Since $\lambda$ is dominant, all these pairings are $\ge0$, so $v$ has no pole along any irreducible component of $G\setminus\Omega$; a rational function on the affine variety $G$ whose pole divisor has no codimension-one component is regular. The identification of $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)$ with the functions satisfying the functional equation is [[lem-sections-of-an-associated-line-bundle-as-equivariant-functions]].

items.title: The nilradical invariants of an irreducible module form its lowest weight line
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, fixed positive system, negative nilradical $\mathfrak n^-$ and Weyl vector $\rho$, and let $\mu$ be a dominant integral weight. Then the space of $\mathfrak n^-$-invariants of the finite-dimensional irreducible module $L(\mu)$ is one-dimensional and equals its lowest weight space: $$\dim L(\mu)^{\mathfrak n^-}=1,\qquad L(\mu)^{\mathfrak n^-}=L(\mu)_{w_0\mu},$$ the lowest weight being $w_0\mu$.
items.strategy: Dualize: the pairing $L(\mu)\times L(\mu)^*\to\mathbb C$ identifies $L(\mu)^{\mathfrak n^-}$ with the annihilator of $\mathfrak n^-L(\mu)^*$. By [[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]] the dual $L(\mu)^*$ is irreducible of highest weight $-w_0\mu$, and by [[prop-the-highest-weight-space-of-an-irreducible-module-is-one-dimensional]] its highest weight space is one-dimensional; a highest weight vector is killed by $\mathfrak n^+$ and is nonzero, so $\mathfrak n^-L(\mu)^*$ has codimension one, spanned by all other weight spaces (weights of $L(\mu)^*$ lie below $-w_0\mu$ and each nonzero-weight-carrying vector can be raised by a positive root chain to the top). Hence $L(\mu)^{\mathfrak n^-}$ is the annihilator of a codimension-one subspace and is itself one-dimensional; its weight is the unique weight of $L(\mu)$ killed by $\mathfrak n^-$, namely the lowest weight $w_0\mu$, because the lowest weight space is one-dimensional and $\mathfrak n^-$-invariant while any other weight vector is moved by a negative simple root by [[lem-highest-weight-modules-have-weights-below-the-top-weight]] and [[def-highest-weight-vector-and-highest-weight-module]].

items.title: Borel-Weil theorem
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$. If $\lambda$ is not dominant integral then $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$. If $\lambda$ is dominant integral then $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong L(\lambda)^*$ as $\mathfrak g$-modules, and $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for every $i>0$.
items.strategy: First compute $H^0$. By [[lem-sections-of-an-associated-line-bundle-as-equivariant-functions]] and [[prop-left-translation-makes-line-bundle-cohomology-a-g-module]] the space $V=H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module, so by [[thm-weyls-complete-reducibility-theorem]] and [[thm-highest-weight-classification-of-finite-dimensional-irreducible-representations]] it is a direct sum $V=\bigoplus_j L(\mu_j)$ of irreducibles with dominant integral highest weights $\mu_j$. By [[lem-lowest-weight-space-is-the-nilradical-invariant-line]] each summand contributes a one-dimensional space of $\mathfrak n^-$-invariants, so $\dim V^{\mathfrak n^-}$ equals the number of summands; [[lem-a-nonzero-dominant-section-is-determined-on-the-big-cell]] bounds this number by one, and [[lem-the-borel-weil-section-extends-from-the-big-cell-to-the-flag-variety]] shows it is exactly one when $\lambda$ is dominant. In that case the nonzero $\mathfrak n^-$-invariant section has $T$-weight $-\lambda$ by the same lemma, while the lowest weight of $L(\mu_1)$ is $w_0\mu_1$; hence $w_0\mu_1=-\lambda$, that is $\mu_1=-w_0\lambda$, and $V\cong L(\mu_1)\cong L(\lambda)^*$. If $\lambda$ were not dominant and $V\neq0$, the same computation would make $\mu_1=-w_0\lambda$ dominant, hence also $\lambda$ dominant because $-w_0$ permutes the simple roots, a contradiction; so $V=0$. For the higher cohomology when $\lambda$ is dominant, apply the wall-crossing isomorphisms of [[lem-rank-one-cohomology-shifts-across-a-simple-wall]] along the chain of [[lem-a-regular-weight-has-a-unique-dominant-dot-translate]] that carries $\lambda$ to the antidominant translate $w_0\cdot\lambda$: each simple reflection moves up one cohomological degree, and the chain has length $|\Phi^+|=N$, so $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong H^{i+N}(X,\mathcal L_{w_0\cdot\lambda})$ for all $i\ge0$; for $i>0$ the target degree exceeds $N=\dim X$, where the cohomology of a locally free sheaf vanishes by [[thm-serre-duality-smooth-projective-variety-locally-free-sheaves]]. The chain step is legal because a dominant weight pairs nonnegatively with every simple coroot, and the step count is $N$ by [[lem-a-regular-weight-has-a-unique-dominant-dot-translate]] applied to the regular weight $\lambda+\rho$ (regular for dominant $\lambda$).

items.title: Rank-one cohomology shifts across a simple wall
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\alpha$ be a simple root and $\lambda\in X^*(T)$, and put $n=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$. If $n\ge-1$, then for every $i\ge0$ there is a natural $G$-equivariant isomorphism $$H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong H^{i+1}(X,\mathcal L_{s_\alpha\cdot\lambda}),$$ where $s_\alpha\cdot\lambda=s_\alpha(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. If $n=-1$ then $s_\alpha\cdot\lambda=\lambda$ and $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for all $i\ge0$. Consequently for every $\lambda$: if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ge-1$ the displayed isomorphism holds, while if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\le-1$ then $H^{i+1}(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong H^i(X,\mathcal L_{s_\alpha\cdot\lambda})$ for all $i\ge0$.
items.strategy: Let $f:X\to X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha$ be the minimal-parabolic projection of [[thm-minimal-parabolic-flag-projection-is-p1-bundle]], a Zariski locally trivial $\mathbb P^1$-bundle by [[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]]. By [[lem-flag-line-bundle-degree-on-minimal-parabolic-fibre]] the restriction of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ to every fibre has degree $n$, so for $n\ge-1$ the relative shift theorem [[thm-relative-p1-line-bundle-cohomology-shift]] applies: $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong H^{i+1}(X,\mathcal L_\lambda\otimes\omega_{(X/X_\alpha)}^{\otimes(n+1)})$, with all maps natural and $G$-equivariant because all constructions are. By [[lem-minimal-parabolic-relative-canonical-line-bundle-root-weight]] the relative canonical bundle is $\omega_{(X/X_\alpha)}\cong\mathcal L_{-\alpha}$, so $\mathcal L_\lambda\otimes\omega_{(X/X_\alpha)}^{\otimes(n+1)}\cong\mathcal L_{\lambda-(n+1)\alpha}=\mathcal L_{s_\alpha\cdot\lambda}$ using $s_\alpha\cdot\lambda=\lambda-(\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle+1)\alpha$ and the tensor rule of [[def-borel-character-equivariant-line-bundle]]. The degenerate case is the $n=-1$ clause of [[lem-relative-projective-line-cohomology-and-apolarity]]: both sheaves in the apolarity isomorphism vanish, and the Leray spectral sequence of [[thm-leray-spectral-sequence-for-sheaf-cohomology]] gives $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for all $i$. The 'consequently' direction is the same statement applied to $s_\alpha\cdot\lambda$, whose coroot pairing is $-n-2$.

items.title: Singular dot weights have zero line-bundle cohomology
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$ and suppose that $\lambda+\rho$ lies on a Weyl wall, that is $\langle\lambda+\rho,\beta^\vee\rangle=0$ for some root $\beta$ (equivalently, $\lambda+\rho$ is not regular, so $\lambda$ is not dot-regular). Equivalently, let $\eta^+$ be the unique point of the $W$-orbit of $\lambda+\rho$ in the closed dominant chamber; then $\langle\eta^+,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=0$ for some simple root $\alpha_i$. The dominant orbit point is unique even when the Weyl element carrying $\lambda+\rho$ to it is not. In this case $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for every $i\ge0$, so all cohomology of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ vanishes and $\mathcal L_\lambda$ is not the geometric realisation of an irreducible representation.
items.strategy: Let $\eta=\lambda+\rho$. While its current Weyl translate is not dominant, reflect across a simple wall with negative pairing; the negative-root count drops by one, so this reaches the unique dominant orbit point. Singularity is preserved, and the terminal dominant singular point has zero pairing with a simple coroot. The rank-one vanishing at that wall and the preceding cohomology shifts give $H^q(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for $q\ge m$, where $m$ is the initial negative-root count. For the remaining degrees, set $\mu=-\lambda-2\rho$ and use the same chain for $-\eta$: its count $m\prime$ satisfies $m+m\prime\le|\Phi^+|-1$ because at least one root pairing vanishes. Serre duality identifies each low-degree group of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ with a complementary group of $\mathcal L_\mu$ above $m\prime$, which vanishes.

items.title: Regular weights have a unique dominant dot translate and monotone wall-crossing chains
items.statement: Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$ with $\mu=\lambda+\rho$ regular, and put $N(\mu)=\#\{\alpha\in\Phi^+:\langle\mu,\alpha^\vee\rangle<0\}$. Then: (i) there is a unique $w\in W$ with $w\mu$ dominant, equivalently a unique $w$ with $w\cdot\lambda$ dominant, and $N(\mu)=\ell(w)$; (ii) if $\alpha$ is simple with $\langle\mu,\alpha^\vee\rangle<0$ then $N(s_\alpha\mu)=N(\mu)-1$, while if $\langle\mu,\alpha^\vee\rangle>0$ then $N(s_\alpha\mu)=N(\mu)+1$; (iii) consequently there is a reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\ell}}$ with $\ell=N(\mu)$ such that the partial products $w_j=s_{i_j}\cdots s_{i_1}$ satisfy $N(w_j\mu)=N(\mu)-j$ and $w_j\mu$ is regular for every $j$, and there is a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_N}$ of the longest element such that the partial products satisfy $N(\cdot)=j$ and end at the strictly antidominant weight $w_0\mu$; (iv) for every $w\in W$ one has $\ell(w_0w)=|\Phi^+|-\ell(w)$. This lemma is choice-free.
items.strategy: (i) A regular weight lies in a unique open chamber, and W acts simply transitively on open chambers. For the unique w with wμ in the fundamental chamber, W-invariance of pairings gives N(μ)=#{α∈Φ+: wα∈Φ−}=ℓ(w); integrality and <ρ,α_i∨>=1 transfer dominance between wμ and w·λ. (ii) A simple reflection permutes the positive roots other than its simple root, so only that root changes the sign count. (iii) Reflect a regular weight across a simple wall with negative (respectively positive) simple pairing to reduce (respectively increase) N by one; chamber uniqueness and the length count show the resulting expressions are reduced and end at the dominant or antidominant chamber. (iv) Count inversion roots of w0w to obtain ℓ(w0w)=|Φ+|−ℓ(w).

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$. If $\lambda+\rho$ is not regular, then $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for all $i\ge0$. u-(\langle
u,\alpha^\veeangle+1)\alpha$ also shows that the shifts agree with the dot action, so the result depends only on $w$.

items.title: Borel-Weil-Bott is compatible with Serre duality
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$ and put $\mu=-\lambda-2\rho$, so that $\mathcal L_\lambda^\vee\otimes K_X\cong\mathcal L_\mu$ by [[lem-flag-variety-canonical-bundle-weight-minus-two-rho]]. Then: (i) $\lambda+\rho$ is regular if and only if $\mu+\rho=-(\lambda+\rho)$ is regular, and if $\lambda+\rho$ is regular with Weyl element $w$ (so $w(\lambda+\rho)$ is dominant) then the Weyl element of $\mu$ is $u=w_0w$, with $\ell(u)=N-\ell(w)$, $N=|\Phi^+|$; (ii) for regular $\lambda$ the Serre pairing $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)^\vee\cong H^{N-i}(X,\mathcal L_\mu)$ at $i=\ell(w)$ identifies $H^{\ell(w)}(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)^\vee$ with $H^{N-\ell(w)}(X,\mathcal L_\mu)\cong L(w\cdot\lambda)$; and the Borel-Weil-Bott descriptions $H^{\ell(w)}(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\lambda)^*$ and $H^{\ell(u)}(X,\mathcal L_\mu)\cong L(u\cdot\mu)^*\cong L(w\cdot\lambda)$ match under this pairing; (iii) if $\lambda+\rho$ is singular then all cohomology groups of both $\mathcal L_\lambda$ and $\mathcal L_\mu$ vanish.
items.strategy:
(i) is immediate from $\mu+ho=-(\lambda+ho)$: regularity is $\pm$-invariant, and $u(\mu+ho)=-w_0w(\lambda+ho)$ is dominant because $w(\lambda+ho)$ is dominant; uniqueness of the Weyl element comes from [[lem-a-regular-weight-has-a-unique-dominant-dot-translate]], and $\ell(w_0w)=N-\ell(w)$ is clause (iv) of that lemma. (ii) On the $w$-side, [[thm-borel-weil-bott]] gives $H^{\ell(w)}(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\lambda)^*$ and on the $\mu$-side, since $u\cdot\mu=u(\mu+ho)-ho=-w_0w(\lambda+ho)-ho=-w_0(w\cdot\lambda)$, it gives $H^{N-\ell(w)}(X,\mathcal L_\mu)\cong L(u\cdot\mu)^*=L(-w_0(w\cdot\lambda))^*$, and $L(-w_0
u)^*\cong L(
u)$ by [[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]] applied twice. Serre duality is [[thm-serre-duality-smooth-projective-variety-locally-free-sheaves]] for the locally free sheaf $\mathcal L_\lambda$ with $\mathcal L_\lambda^\vee\otimes\omega_X\cong\mathcal L_{-\lambda-2ho}$. (iii) The singular condition is preserved by $
u\mapsto-
u$ by (i), and both vanishing statements are [[thm-borel-weil-bott]].

items.title: The Borel-Weil-Bott Euler character is a signed dual Weyl character
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathrm{ch}$
denote the formal character of a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module
([[def-formal-character-of-a-finite-dimensional-weight-module]]) and let $A$
be the Weyl alternation operator with Weyl denominator
$A(\rho)=\prod_{\alpha>0}(e^{\alpha/2}-e^{-\alpha/2})$
([[def-weyl-alternation-operator]], [[thm-weyl-character-formula]]). For every $\lambda\in X^*(T)$: if
$\lambda+\rho$ is not regular then
$\sum_i(-1)^i\mathrm{ch}\,H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$; if $\lambda+\rho$ is
regular with Weyl element $w$, then
$$\sum_i(-1)^i\mathrm{ch}\,H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\mathrm{ch}\,L(w\cdot\lambda)^*=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\frac{A(-w_0(w\cdot\lambda)+\rho)}{A(\rho)}.$$
Equivalently, with $\nu=-w_0(w\cdot\lambda)$, which is the dominant integral
weight of the dual module $L(w\cdot\lambda)^*$, the last expression is
$(-1)^{\ell(w)}A(\nu+\rho)/A(\rho)$.
items.strategy: Apply thm-borel-weil-bott and additivity of formal characters: singular shifted weights give zero; a regular shifted weight contributes only (-1)^ell(w) ch L(w dot lambda)^*. The dominant integral highest weight of this dual is nu=-w0(w dot lambda). Apply thm-weyl-character-formula at nu to get (-1)^ell(w) A(nu+rho)/A(rho). The denominator identity comes from that theorem; the half-root product follows from rho being half the sum of positive roots. Weyl invariance is not used to remove the dual.

title: Borel Weil and Borel Weil Bott — Examples

items.title: The sl2 singular weight has no cohomology
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For $G=SL_2(\mathbb C)$ the weight $\lambda=-\rho=-\omega_1$ has $\lambda+\rho=0$ on the Weyl wall, and $\mathcal L_{-\omega_1}\cong\mathcal O(-1)$ on $X\cong\mathbb P^1$. All cohomology of $\mathcal L_{-\omega_1}$ vanishes: $H^0(X,\mathcal L_{-\omega_1})=H^1(X,\mathcal L_{-\omega_1})=0$. More generally the wall-crossing isomorphism $H^i(X,\mathcal L_{-\omega_1})\cong H^{i+1}(X,\mathcal L_{-\omega_1})$ of [[lem-rank-one-cohomology-shifts-across-a-simple-wall]] together with the vanishing above degree $1$ forces every cohomology group to vanish.
items.strategy: Compute the pairing: $\langle-\omega_1,\alpha^\vee\rangle=-1$, so $s\cdot(-\omega_1)=-\omega_1$ and $\lambda+\rho=0$; by [[thm-serre-duality-smooth-projective-variety-locally-free-sheaves]] (or [[ex-cohomology-o-d-projective-line-all-d]]) $h^0=h^1=0$ for the twist $-1$. The consistency argument: [[lem-rank-one-cohomology-shifts-across-a-simple-wall]] gives a natural isomorphism $H^i\cong H^{i+1}$ for all $i\ge0$; since $H^i=0$ for $i>1=\dim X$ by the same Serre-duality item, descending from $i=1$ gives $H^1\cong H^2=0$ and then $H^0\cong H^1=0$. This is the sharp boundary value $n=-1$ of the rank-one shift and the smallest instance of [[lem-singular-dot-weights-have-zero-line-bundle-cohomology]].

items.title: Borel-Weil-Bott on the projective line for SL2
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G=SL_2(\mathbb C)$ with upper triangular Borel $B$ and flag variety $X=G/B\cong\mathbb P^1$, and for $m\in\mathbb Z$ let $\mathcal L_{m\omega_1}=G\times^B\mathbb C_{-m\omega_1}\cong\mathcal O(m)$ be the line bundles of [[ex-sl2-flag-variety-line-bundles]]. Then, with $L(m\omega_1)$ the irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $m\omega_1$: (i) for $m\ge0$, $H^0(X,\mathcal L_{m\omega_1})\cong L(m\omega_1)^*$ and $H^1(X,\mathcal L_{m\omega_1})=0$; (ii) for $m\le-2$, $H^1(X,\mathcal L_{m\omega_1})\cong L((-m-2)\omega_1)^*$ and $H^0(X,\mathcal L_{m\omega_1})=0$; (iii) for $m=-1$, $H^0(X,\mathcal L_{-\omega_1})=H^1(X,\mathcal L_{-\omega_1})=0$. The Borel-Weil-Bott degree is $0$ for $m\ge0$, $1$ for $m\le-2$, and the weight $m\omega_1$ is singular exactly for $m=-1$.
items.strategy: In rank one $\rho=\omega_1$, so $\lambda+\rho=(m+1)\omega_1$ is regular exactly for $m\ne-1$, and for $m\ge0$ the Weyl element is $1$ while for $m\le-2$ it is $s$ with $s\cdot(m\omega_1)=-(m+2)\omega_1$. Apply [[thm-borel-weil-bott]] and use the identification with twists: (i) and (ii) are then the classical table $\dim H^0(\mathcal O(m))=\max(m+1,0)$, $\dim H^1(\mathcal O(m))=\max(-m-1,0)$ of [[ex-cohomology-o-d-projective-line-all-d]] together with $\dim L(k\omega_1)=k+1$; (iii) is [[ex-the-sl2-singular-weight-has-no-cohomology]]. The line-bundle identifications are those proved in [[ex-sl2-flag-variety-line-bundles]].

items.title: An sl3 weight with cohomology in degree one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G=SL_3(\mathbb C)$ with standard Borel, simple roots $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$, fundamental weights $\omega_1,\omega_2$ and $\rho=\omega_1+\omega_2$, and put $\lambda=s_1\cdot\rho=\rho-2\alpha_1=-3\omega_1+3\omega_2$. Then $\lambda+\rho=s_1(2\rho)$ is regular with Weyl element $w=s_1$ and $s_1\cdot\lambda=\rho$, so [[thm-borel-weil-bott]] gives $H^1(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong L(\rho)^*$ and $H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for $i\neq1$. Since $L(\rho)$ is the eight-dimensional adjoint representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, $H^1$ is eight-dimensional and the Euler-characteristic formula reads $\mathrm{ch}\,H^0-\mathrm{ch}\,H^1=-\mathrm{ch}\,L(\rho)$.
items.strategy: Compute in the $A_2$ root data: $\rho=\omega_1+\omega_2$ is strictly dominant ($\langle\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=1$), so $2\rho$ is regular and $s_1(2\rho)$ is again regular; $\lambda=s_1\cdot\rho$ satisfies $s_1\cdot\lambda=\rho$, and $\ell(s_1)=1$. The Borel-Weil-Bott conclusion is then the statement of [[thm-borel-weil-bott]] at this weight, and the dimension is that of [[ex-the-eight-dimensional-adjoint-representation-of-sl-three]]; the dual $L(\rho)^*$ has the same dimension and is isomorphic to $L(\rho)$ because the adjoint representation is self-dual. The Euler-characteristic form is [[cor-borel-weil-bott-euler-character-is-the-weyl-character]].

items.title: The top-degree Borel-Weil-Bott case and Serre duality
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G=SL_3(\mathbb C)$ with $\rho=\omega_1+\omega_2$, let $N=3=|\Phi^+|$ and put $\lambda=w_0\cdot\rho=-3\rho$, so that $\lambda+\rho=-2\rho$ is regular with Weyl element $w_0$ and $w_0\cdot\lambda=\rho$. Then [[thm-borel-weil-bott]] gives $$H^3(X,\mathcal L_{-3\rho})\cong L(\rho)^*,\qquad H^i(X,\mathcal L_{-3\rho})=0\ (i\neq3),$$ and the Serre pairing $$H^3(X,\mathcal L_{-3\rho})\times H^0(X,\mathcal L_{\rho})\longrightarrow H^3(X,K_X)\cong\mathbb C$$ is perfect; both sides are eight-dimensional. This is the $w=w_0$, top-degree case of [[prop-borel-weil-bott-is-compatible-with-serre-duality]] with $\mu=-\lambda-2\rho=\rho$ and $u=w_0w_0=1$.
items.strategy: Since $\rho$ is strictly dominant, $w_0\rho=-\rho$ and $\lambda=w_0\cdot\rho=w_0(2\rho)-\rho=-3\rho$; then $\lambda+\rho=-2\rho$, $w_0(\lambda+\rho)=2\rho$ is dominant, and $w_0\cdot\lambda=w_0(-2\rho)-\rho=2\rho-\rho=\rho$, so the Weyl element is $w_0$ with $\ell(w_0)=3=N$; apply [[thm-borel-weil-bott]]. For the pairing, $\mu=-\lambda-2\rho=3\rho-2\rho=\rho$ and [[lem-flag-variety-canonical-bundle-weight-minus-two-rho]] identifies $\mathcal L_{-3\rho}^\vee\otimes K_X\cong\mathcal L_{3\rho-2\rho}=\mathcal L_\rho$; [[thm-serre-duality-smooth-projective-variety-locally-free-sheaves]] gives the perfect pairing and [[prop-borel-weil-bott-is-compatible-with-serre-duality]] identifies both factors; the dimension is that of the adjoint module [[ex-the-eight-dimensional-adjoint-representation-of-sl-three]].

items.title: Changing the line-bundle sign changes the Borel-Weil section space
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For G=SL_2(C) and an integer m>0, the library bundle L_(m omega_1) is O(m), whereas the opposite fibre-character convention gives L_(-m omega_1)=O(-m). Their H0 spaces have dimensions m+1 and 0 respectively. The sign change dualizes the line bundle; it does not dualize the space of sections.
items.strategy: Use def-borel-character-equivariant-line-bundle to identify the opposite convention with L_(-lambda), and lem-flag-line-bundle-degree-on-minimal-parabolic-fibre to identify the rank-one twists. thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves gives H0(O(-m))=0 for m>0; thm-borel-weil gives the nonzero dual irreducible module for L_(m omega_1). No higher-cohomology vanishing for O(-m) is asserted.
